spiritual_reading:
#
 Spiritual
 Translation
 of
 the Kephalaia Chapter


---


**
¶2:** It
 is the entrance
 into
 spiritual
 life and
 the containing form of divine peace,
 opening
 toward
 the
 great heav
enly state
 of wisdom
 itself
.

**¶4:** In
 every renewed
 state of the
 spirit
, the Divine
 Love and Wisdom proce
eding from the Lord communic
ates itself,
 and it
 produces
 the fullness of spiritual blessings
 for
 those
 who receive it. Can
 they not perceive these with their
 understanding?

**¶5:**
 The first blessing
 it
 best
ows is wisdom
 itself
, which it p
ours into the understanding
.
 It opens the inner
 sight
 of
 all people
. They perce
ive the
 tru
ths beneath their feet —
 the path of life on
 which they walk —
 by
 means
 of that
 wisdom. It disp
els the ignorance of
 the state
 of
 spiritual darkness,
 which had
 closed
 their understanding
 with
 its fals
ity.

**¶6:**
 The second:
 When Divine
 Wisdom enters the mind, its
 coming
 brings tranquility and inner peace to
 the whole
 person.
 With
 its coming it also
 removes
 from
 them the
 anxiety
 and dread with
 which their
 will
 was
 filled during the
 entire
 state of spiritual darkness;
 for it displ
aces the fals
ity present
 in
 the mind
 by
 means
 of truth
,
 and sweeps it out entirely
. And
 in
 this same
 way it extinguishes anxiety
 by means
 of its peace
.

**¶7:** The
 third is its
 awak
ening power
; because when Divine Wisdom enters the
 mind, all who were in spiritual torp
or arise into active spiritual life. And
 the tru
ths that stood
 guard during
 the night
 of the
 understanding
 —
 the protective
 cogn
itions stationed
 at
 the entr
ances to the mind — they may
 rest from their anxious vigil
ance, because wisdom itself
 now illuminates the whole
 interior
.


**¶8:** The fourth
: It nourishes and
 gives vit
ality,
 substance
, and de
light to all
 perceptions and
 their
 resulting
 works
,
 to
 all natural
 knowledges and developing
 cogn
itions, and
 to every
 bud
ding insight
 and living
 thought
 that
 exists
 upon
 the whole
 ground
 of the
 natural
 mind.

**¶9:**
 The fifth: When Divine Wisdom sh
ines throughout
 the whole
 mind
, the lowest
 sens
ual falsities and the fierce selfish
 affections that
 are filled with mal
ice —
 they flee and
 conc
eal themselves in their hidden interior
 rec
esses.


**¶10:** The sixth
: When its
 truth
 sh
ines forth
, the spiritual injury
 of
 every
 person is e
ased of
 its
 suffering
. Its wisdom
 dissol
ves the deceptive arts of every
 worker
 of evil.

**¶11
:** The seventh: Divine
 Wisdom displays
 and
 makes
 manifest to
 the mind
 the sign of the glory
 of the heavenly states
 from which it has proceeded
; it being
,
 here
 in the
 natural
 mind, their
 representative
 image
. It brings wisdom
 to the whole of the
 created
 order.

---


**¶13:** The state
 of spiritual darkness —
 for
 it contains all evils within it.
 Every time spiritual darkness descends upon the
 mind, it produces the fullness of
 evil in
 the whole person.

**¶
14:** The first evil that
 spiritual darkness works
 in
 the mind is falsity,
 with
 which it fills the entire person
;
 because
 when Divine Wisdom withdraws from
 the mind and gathers back
 into
 itself its emanating
 rays
 of
 truth
, at
 that instant the shadow of ignor
ance spreads over the whole interior
.
 The understanding of
 the
 people
 fills
 with obsc
urity. They neither perce
ive nor app
rehend anything
 with their inner
 sight
, because of the fals
ity of spiritual
 darkness which fills the whole mind.


**¶15:** The second evil
 that spiritual darkness works is
 d
read;
 because when its shadow looms forth,
 its anxiety
 and its trembling se
ize the whole will
 of a
 person. The entire
 mind fills with the night
 of the
 understanding
.

**¶16:** The
 third: When spiritual darkness falls, all
 affections rise
 up in rebellion. They
 turn
 in
 the
 will toward evil and destruction.

**
¶17:** The fourth:
 The heav
iness of spiritual
 torp
or l
ays upon them, and they fall into
 unconsc
iousness of
 spirit
; they grow
 ins
ensible
 and dull, and they are like
 the
 spiritu
ally dead in
 the state
 of inner
 darkness
.

**¶18:** The
 fifth is
 its de
formity; again, when spiritual darkness
 desc
ends, the true
 form of every
 person is conce
aled in the fals
ity and
 ugl
iness of ignor
ance. The spiritual
 beauty and the
 living
 form that
 good
 and truth compose in
 men
 and women cannot
 be displayed
 to
 one another nor
 recognized
,
 because of the
 falsity and
 de
formity which
 it spreads over all their interior
 forms.

**¶19:**
 The sixth occasion is when spiritual darkness falls
 upon
 the mind
. At that instant those
 ruled
 by evil come forth to work
 their
 ev
ils:
 those who falsify truths,
 those
 who steal the goods of faith, and
 those who corrupt truths with subtle poison
. The fierce
 selfish affections come
 forth, and all the sensual fals
ities that are filled with mal
ice, from
 their hidden interiors.
 And they
 stalk through
 the dark
ened mind
. Also
, the infernal spirits and the
 powers
 of hell
 gain the
 strength
 to work evil
 in the night of
 the
 understanding.
 Again, the blows and ass
aults and spiritual
 injuries
 and eru
ptions of evil
 torment the person
 in that
 darkness; because in it the whole of
 evil finds
 its
 power
.

**¶20:** The
 seventh:
 Spiritual darkness displays the sign
 of
 Pr
imal Falsity,
 its
 origin
.
 It has arisen from its very
 essence; because this night of
 the understanding that
 issued from the
 original
 Falsity has been made
 manifest in the mind
.
 Behold this spiritual
 darkness
 —
 the shadow of that
 original evil, the
 one that is interwoven and bound
 in all things of the mind, both
 interior and exterior.

---


**¶22:** There
 are five essential
 qualities present
 in the Divine
 Wisdom
,
 which
 it produces
 as
 it encounters
 the state
 of the
 mind
.


**¶23:** The first
 is its truth
; for
 it illuminates
 the mind by its truth, and all
 the aff
ections and
 thoughts
 that exist ther
ein.

**¶24:**
 The second is its beauty; because when
 it shines, it floods the form
 of good
ness and spiritual
 lo
veliness upon all aff
ections and upon
 everything in
 the mind.

**¶25
:** The third is its peace; for
, again, when Divine
 Wisdom shines upon the mind,
 all the
 fac
ulties of the person
 receive
 mutual
 love
 through
 it, and give peace to one another
.

**¶26:** The
 fourth is the liberation
 of the living soul,
 which it releases from all the bonds and
 constraints
 that
 heaven and earth —
 the interior
 and the exterior of
 the person
 — had
 imposed upon it.

**¶
27:** The fifth: It gives power
 to the fundamental
 principles of spiritual
 life; and also
 it gives sa
vor and substance
 to the universal order of divine truth distributed
 throughout
 all
 creation.

**¶28:**
 Its
 truth
 illuminates
 more than all particular
 truths that occur
 in the mind
. Also
, its beauty is more beautiful than all
 the forms
 of good
ness in hum
ankind. Again, its peace sur
passes all the protective
 powers and guardian
 tru
ths that exist in the mind. Its
 liber
ating action, by which it releases the
 living soul, is a full degree
 beyond
 all other
 acts
 of liberation
.
 The strength
 that it gives to its members
 is a great power
, m
ightier than all other
 powers
.


---


**¶29:** Once again
, there are another
 three essential
 qualities made
 apparent by Divine
 Wisdom,
 in respect of the mystery of the Divine
 Itself.

**¶30:**
 The first is the perpet
ual full
ness of the containing
 form
 of its proce
eding love
; because its vessel
 is
 filled in
 every state
 and
 never
 dimin
ishes at
 all, in
 the way that the vessel
 of reflected
 faith
 dimin
ishes. This continuous full
ness, by which it is sustained
, displays the mystery of the Divine
 Itself, the
 Infinite Good, from whom
 all the powers and the heav
enly
 beings have proceeded
. He never
 diminishes, nor does any
 lack ever exist in Him
.


**¶31:** The second
: The wisdom
 of the Divine proce
eding surpasses the wisdom of all
 particular
 knowledges,
 and all
 the tru
ths that occur
 in the whole
 of creation;
 corresponding to the mystery of the truth
 of the Divine Itself;
 for His
 wisdom surpasses and is greater than
 the wisdom of all the heav
enly societies
.

**¶32:** The
 third: The
 Divine
 Wisdom is elevated
 far
 above all else. It surpasses
 the height of all the ex
alted states
 of love and all
 the elevated
 aff
ections of charity that
 exist upon
 the whole
 ground
 of the mind —
 corresponding to the mystery of the
 Infinite Good
; for He is ex
alted above the
 whole
 household of His heaven
.
 Also, because the Divine
 Itself is high
 above all the heights and elevated
 states of His celest
ial kingdom. He is full
 in
 His image through
 all time
 and every moment
 from eternity to eternity.


---


**¶34:** The mystery
 of the first and
 infinite
 Wisdom is the Divine
 Love
 and Wisdom proceeding from the Lord
,
 which is that
 second and
 manifest
 light,
 the
 one that enters
 daily
 into every
 state
 of the mind.
 It displays all the marks of its b
lessings, manif
esting and signifying on its own behalf
 that it is Good
, out
 of the essence of the Good. It
 came forth
 from the Good that
 is the Divine
 Itself,
 and appeared in this world.

**
¶35:** In contrast, this
 spiritual
 darkness
 that is comp
ounded
 of d
read exists
 as
 the image
 of primal Falsity.
 Behold also
 the mystery of its essence! It displays
 itself
 in the mind
 in all these ev
ils.

reconstructions.reconstructed_text: it is the gate of life and the vessel of peace, to this great aeon of light [of the Father of Greatness].
Every day, would this great light-giver shine its light, it shall do seven good things for them. Shall they not see them?

The first good thing that it does for them is its light, which it shines upon them. It opens the eyes of all mankind. They see underfoot as they walk by it. It takes away the blindness of the night, which made them blind with its darkness.

The second: When (the Sun) is come to the world, with its coming it shall bring calm and peace to the entire world. With its coming it shall also take away from them all the fear and trembling, which their heart is filled with the whole night; for it shall take away the darkness present by its light, and sweep it out. Also, this is how it extinguishes fear by its calm.

The third is its vigil; because when (the Sun) comes to the world all sleeping mankind shall arise and awake. And the watchmen too shall cease from watching. The guards who sit at the gates of camps, they break vigil at the watchposts, because of its light that has shone upon them in the world.
The fourth: It shall nourish, and give strength, taste and scent, to the trees and fruits and vegetables, and all the herbs, and the flowers and grasses, which are upon the entire earth.
The fifth: When (the Sun) shines in all the world, the evil reptile and the sharp-toothed beasts that are filled of wickedness, they shall flee to hiding in their dens.
The sixth: When it shines its light, the wound of any person is eased from pain. Its light shall melt away the evil arts of every doer of wickedness.

The seventh: (The Sun) shall display and manifest to the world the sign of the splendour of the aeons of light, from which it has come out; it here in this world being their sign. It brings light to the whole of creation.

The first wickedness that the Night shall do in the world is the darkness, with which it shall fill the entire world; because when the sun sinks from the world and draws to it its rays, at that instant the shadow of the night shall spread out over the whole world. The eyes of the people fill with blackness. They neither see nor wonder with their eyes, because of the darkness of the night which shall fill the whole world.
The second evil thing that the Night shall do is its fear; because when its shadow looms forth, its fear and its trembling shall possess all of mankind. The entire world shall fill of the night.
The third: When the Night falls, all creatures take up revolt. They rebel in their heart, to do wickedness and perdition.
The fourth: The heaviness of sleep shall lay upon them, and they fall asleep; they slumber and doze, and they are like these corpses in the night.

The fifth is its ugliness; again, when the Night would fall, the form of the people shall be hidden in the darkness and the ugliness of the night. The beauty and the form of men and women shall not be displayed before one another, because of its darkness and its ugliness, which it shall spread out over all their forms.

The sixth occasion is when the Night would fall on the world. At that instant evil people shall come out to do wickedness; the adulterers, and the robbers and poisoners. The evil beasts shall come out, and all the reptiles that are filled with wickedness, from their dens. And they stalk in the night. Also, the demons and fiends find power to do wickedness in the night. Again, the blows and buffets and wounds and discharges shall torment people in the night; because in it the whole of evil shall find strength.

The seventh: The Night shall display the sign of the Darkness, its father. It has arisen out of its essence; because this night that came out of this first Darkness has been displayed in the world. Note this night, the shadow of this first Darkness, the one that is entwined and bound in all things above and below.
There are five archetypes occur in the Sun, it making them [apparent] as it finds the world.
The first is its light; for it illumines by its light the world, and all the creatures who exist in it.
The second is its beauty; because when it shines, it shall flood beauty and loveliness upon all creatures and everything.
The third is its peace; for, again, when the sun would shine on the world, all people shall receive affection through it, and give peace to one another.
The fourth is the life of the Living Soul, which it shall release from all the bonds and fetters of heaven and earth.
The fifth: It gives a strength to the elements; and also it gives a scent and a taste to the entire Cross of the Light.
Once again, there are another three archetypes made apparent by the sun, in respect of the mystery of the first greatness.

The first is the filling up of the disk of its ship; because its ship has filled up every season, and shall not wane at all, the way that the ship of the moon wanes. This continuous filling, by which it is filled, displays the mystery of the Father, the great greatness; from whom all the powers and the gods have come forth. He shall never wane, nor shall lack ever exist in him!

The second: (The sun's) light surpasses the light of all the stars, and all the lights that occur in the universe; corresponding to the mystery of the light of the Father; for his light surpasses and is greater than the light of his aeons.

The third: This sun is very high above all else. It surpasses the height of all the mountains and hills that exist upon the entire earth, corresponding to the mystery of the Father of Greatness; for he is high above all the household of his light-earth. Also, because the Father himself is high above all the heights and the mountains of his light-earth. He is 'filled up' in his image [all] the time and every hour from eternity to eternity!

The mystery of the first great light is the sun, which is this second light-giver, the one that comes daily to the world. It displays all the marks of its graces, displaying and signifying on its own behalf that it is good, out of the essence of the good. It came from the good Father and appeared in this world.

In contrast, this Night that is made of fear exists after the mystery of the Darkness. Behold too the mystery of its essence! It displays it in the world in all these wickednesses. It displays this mystery daily in the world,
